blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
Introduction 
The AIDS epidemic continues to spread across the South-East Asia (SEA) 
Region, which is the most affected part of the world after sub-Saharan Africa. 
To date, around 40 million people around the world have been infected with 
the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), the virus that causes AIDS. Of them 
more than six million are in the SEA Region. 
The “3 by 5” initiative has stimulated Member States to accelerate and 
strengthen mechanisms for providing antiretroviral therapy (ART) to needy 
people living with HIV. The availability of economical generic drugs has 
further booste

summary.text: Introduces the Bangkok workshop on CD4 T lymphocyte counting, citing the HIV burden in the South-East Asia Region and the need for CD4 testing to guide antiretroviral therapy. It notes that sixteen laboratory professionals from seven countries attended, facilitated by Siriraj Hospital and India's National AIDS Research Institute.

blocks.title: Objectives
blocks.content:
Objectives 
The objectives of the workshop were to: 
(1) Review the status of enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes in high 
HIV-burden Member countries of the SEA Region; 
(2) Orient on new, economical and field-friendly technologies for CD4 
enumeration; 
(3) Provide hands-on training on selected technologies including the 
interpretation of results, and 
(4) Identify a mechanism for external quality assessment scheme.

summary.text: Lists the workshop's four objectives, from reviewing CD4 enumeration status to hands-on training and planning external quality assessment.

blocks.title: Inaugural session
blocks.content:
Inaugural session 
The Dean of the medical faculty at Siriraj Hospital welcomed the participants. 
In his inaugural remarks, he emphasized that CD4 enumeration technology is 
critical for effective implementation of any programme on antiretroviral 
therapy as well as for providing efficient care to the patient. 
Acting WHO Representative, Thailand read the inaugural address of Dr 
Samlee Plianbangchang, Regional Director, WHO South-East Asia (SEA) 
Region. In his inaugural address, Dr Samlee said that the Millennium 
Development Goals (MDGs) have identified HIV as a disease of global

summary.text: Summarizes the opening of the CD4 workshop, where speakers stressed the importance of CD4 counts for antiretroviral treatment and of quality assurance. Participants were encouraged to learn about the various technologies so they could choose one suited to their infrastructure and resources.

summary.text: Outlines the workshop's working methods and then reports on the status of CD4 T lymphocyte enumeration in participating countries such as Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. The country reports cover available equipment, laboratories performing counts, training and participation in quality assessment schemes. Thailand's report notes training courses run by Siriraj Hospital's centre of excellence and a national institute since 2004.

blocks.title: Presentations and topics for discussions
blocks.content:
Presentations and topics for discussions 
Role of CD4 count in HIV infection 
Dr Ramesh Paranjape, Director, National AIDS Research Institute (NARI), 
Pune, India, discussed the immunopathogenesis of HIV infection and the role 
of CD4 count estimation in HIV infection. He gave an account of the infection 
of CD4+ T cells by HIV and the co-receptor usage of HIV for entry in the cell. 
He elaborated the clinical course of HIV infection, different patterns of HIV 
disease progression and mechanisms of CD4 + T cell depletion in HIV 
infection. Dr Paranjape also explained about the use of CD4 count

summary.text: Summarizes the technical presentations at the workshop, beginning with the role of CD4 counts in HIV pathogenesis, disease monitoring and decisions on starting antiretroviral therapy. Further talks explain flow cytometry principles, gating strategies such as panleucogating, low-cost and alternative counting methods, and haematology analysers. It concludes that the choice of method should depend on test volume, staff, support and cost, with validation and proficiency testing before routine use.

blocks.title: Group work
blocks.content:
Group work 
Participants developed a generic plan for the establishment of a national 
external quality assessment scheme for CD4 T lymphocytes enumeration. The 
draft plan emphasized on responsibility of the National Programme Officer to 
institutionalize national EQAS, development of infrastructure for EQAS, 
training of human resource, logistics for shipment of material with or without 
stabilizers, continuous collaboration between the organizer of the scheme as 
well as the participating units and a continuing endeavour towards quality 
improvement.

summary.text: Describes a generic plan drafted by participants for a national external quality assessment scheme for CD4 counting, covering responsibilities, infrastructure, training and specimen logistics.

blocks.title: Hands-on enumeration of CD4 T Lymphocytes
blocks.content:
Hands-on enumeration of CD4 T Lymphocytes 
All participants were demonstrated flow cytometry techniques using 
FACSCount and Tritest on FACSCalibur. The tests were also performed by the

An open session was organized with the participants on the last day of 
the workshop. All subjects that were discussed at the workshop were

summary.text: Notes that participants were shown and performed flow cytometric CD4 counting and that a final open session reviewed topics and country-specific issues.
A heading introducing the workshop's recommendations.

blocks.title: For WHO
blocks.content:
For WHO 
The following actions were recommended for WHO:  
(1) WHO should develop guidelines and standard operating procedure 
for CD4 T lymphocytes enumeration. 
(2) WHO should support the expansion of Regional CD4 T 
lymphocytes EQAS to Sri Lanka, Myanmar, and Nepal in addition to 
India, Indonesia and Thailand where it is already in operation. 
(3) WHO should develop criteria for clinical application of CD4 counts 
in paediatric population.

summary.text: Lists recommendations for WHO, including guidelines and procedures for CD4 enumeration, expansion of the regional quality scheme and criteria for paediatric use.

blocks.title: For Member States
blocks.content:
For Member States 
The following were recommended for Member countries:  
(1) Member countries should accord priority to establish infrastructure 
for CD4 T lymphocytes enumeration to provide effective support to 
ART programmes. 
(2) Member countries should initiate a national EQAS for CD4 T 
lymphocytes and selected laboratories should participate in WHO 
Regional EQAS.

blocks.title: Concluding session
blocks.content:
Concluding session 
WHO’s initiative in organizing this meeting was appreciated in the concluding 
session. The participants also felt that the deliberations shall go a long way in 
developing or improving the laboratory support to ART programmes. The 
meeting ended with a vote of thanks to officials who managed the meeting. 
Dr Rajesh Bhatia thanked the local organizers, Siriraj Hospital and the Ministry 
of Public Health, Thailand, for the conduct of this workshop. He also thanked 
the facilitators, local organizers as well as international experts who facilitated
